title: A Promise for the Harbor
premise: Marine biologist Mara Fairweather retreats to the coastal town of Saltmere Harbor to lick her wounds after a betrayal, only to inherit half of a crumbling apple orchard alongside Elias Thorne — the estranged son of the woman who once took her in, and the man whose family ruined her own. Forced to co-manage the orchard through one harvest season, they move from hostility to wary partnership to love, while a developer's offer and a buried family secret threaten to destroy everything. When the deed's true history surfaces, Mara must choose between selling out her pain and claiming a future. She stays past the last ferry, choosing Elias and the orchard's found family of misfit workers over the safety of leaving.
about_author: Ulyana Joubert spent a decade working seasonal jobs in coastal towns from Nova Scotia to Cornwall, collecting the salt-worn voices that populate her fiction. She writes romances about people who rebuild themselves the way harbors rebuild after storms — slowly, and with a lot of stubborn hope.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reeling from a research grant scandal engineered by her ex-partner, Mara arrives in Saltmere Harbor to house-sit and count sea turtle nests. She catalogs the town's rhythms while refusing to unpack emotionally. Beat: guarded exhaustion, the first breath of a place that might hold her.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A lawyer summons her: her late benefactor, Agnes Thorne, left her half of Fairweather Orchard — named for Mara's own grandmother. The other half belongs to Elias Thorne, Agnes's estranged son. Beat: shock and suspicion; the past has teeth.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Sign
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias returns after twelve years away intending to sell his half fast, and finds Mara already living in his mother's house. Their first collision is over a broken fence and older wounds. Beat: friction, mutual misreading, grudging fascination.

chapters.title: Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They negotiate an uneasy truce: ninety days to harvest, then sell to the highest bidder and part ways. The orchard's ragtag crew — aging foreman Dot, teenager Juniper, and quiet farmhand Sam — watch warily. Beat: a pact built on avoidance.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Working the orchard, Mara learns her grandmother once worked these very rows alongside Agnes Thorne — before a falling-out no one will explain. Elias stonewalls her questions. Beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A September gale threatens the crop; Mara wades into flooded rows to save the irrigation pump, and Elias drags her out half-drowned. Soaked and furious, they laugh for the first time together. Beat: forced intimacy, the thaw begins.

chapters.title: Juniper's Secret
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara catches Juniper hiding bruises and learns the girl is couch-surfing after fleeing home. Against her own rules about attachment, Mara offers the spare room. Beat: found family takes root; Mara risks caring again.

chapters.title: The Developer's Letter
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A resort developer, Calder Voss, offers a sum that would erase Elias's debts and fund his stalled career — if both heirs sign. Elias hides the letter from Mara. Beat: temptation and the first real lie.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The harvest festival; cider, dancing, and a kiss beneath the oldest apple tree that neither can pretend away. Elias nearly tells Mara about Voss's offer. He doesn't. Beat: sweetness shadowed by the coming fall.

chapters.title: Agnes's Letters
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the attic, Mara finds decades of letters between Agnes and her grandmother — revealing Agnes once destroyed evidence that would have saved Mara's family farm from Elias's father's ruthless land grab. Beat: the enemy has a face, and it's the house she loves.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers Mara has the letters and realizes she knows everything — including that he knew and never told her. He confesses about Voss's offer in the same breath, making it worse. Beat: the rupture; both retreat behind walls.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara packs to leave before the season's final ferry, but Dot reveals the truth of that old betrayal: Elias's father coerced Agnes, and Elias has spent his life paying for it. Mara boards anyway. Beat: lowest point; the truth arrives too late.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone, Elias finally reads Agnes's last letter to him — she left him the orchard not as inheritance but as penance and a chance, and named Mara co-heir deliberately to force them together. Beat: devastating clarity; he chooses to fight.

chapters.title: Voss Moves First
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Voss, tired of waiting, files a claim challenging the deed using the old land-grab documents, threatening the orchard and Juniper's new home. The crew rallies. Beat: external threat crystallizes; enemies become allies.

chapters.title: The Harbor Shows Up
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara returns mid-legal-crisis to find the whole town — fishermen, the ferry captain, Dot's old crew — testifying to the orchard's history. She and Elias work side by side, wordless, rebuilding trust through labor. Beat: found family as fortress.

chapters.title: Turtle Season
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias joins Mara's nighttime nest count, and in the dark she tells him about her ex's betrayal and why she lends out her heart in pieces. He answers with his own account of his father. Beat: raw honesty; the real second chance.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the county hearing, Voss produces a forged signature — Elias's father's old trick. Mara takes the stand and, instead of weaponizing Agnes's letters, testifies to what the orchard means. Beat: Mara chooses grace over revenge; the tide turns.

chapters.title: Verdict and Vow
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The claim collapses; Voss withdraws, exposed. Elias publicly refuses any sale and asks Mara — not the co-heir, the woman — to stay. She says she needs time. Beat: victory without resolution; love must be chosen, not defaulted into.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara returns to her old life briefly — a job offer, an apology from her ex — and finds it fits like a coat she's outgrown. She realizes survival was never the same thing as living. Beat: the internal choice made.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The final ferry departs without her. Mara walks the orchard road at dawn to find Elias and the crew planting new trees in the frozen ground — her grandmother's heirloom grafts, which Elias tracked down. Beat: whole heart, no pieces lent.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Winter settles; Juniper enrolls in school, Dot retires to the porch, and Mara splits her time between the orchard and a new coastal research post. She and Elias amend the deed — both names, deliberately, together. Beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Blossom Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. Spring: the orchard blooms, turtles return to the harbor, and Elias proposes under the oldest tree with a ring made from a grafting knife. Mara says yes before he finishes. Beat: the promise kept; second chances, well-timed after all.
